errors.sentence: He has went to the library twice this week.
errors.explanation: Use the past participle gone after has in the present perfect.

errors.sentence: I look forward to hear from you soon.
errors.explanation: Use a gerund after the phrasal verb look forward to.

errors.sentence: She gave me an advice before the interview.
errors.explanation: Advice is uncountable in English, so use some advice instead.

errors.sentence: Everyone in the office were excited about the new project.
errors.explanation: Everyone is singular, so it takes the singular verb was.

errors.sentence: We are interested on learning how this engine works.
errors.explanation: The adjective interested is followed by the preposition in.
